steps.prompt: Someone flipped sentence A into the passive. Can you spot the two mistakes in B?
steps.b: The fence was painted by she.
steps.reveal: The tense changed (is painting → was painted; it should be “is being painted”), and “she” should be “her” after “by”. A good flip keeps the meaning, the tense and the right pronouns: “The fence is being painted by her.”

cards.title: Active → passive
cards.text:
Our class planted ten trees.
1. The receiver moves to the front: Ten trees…
2. Add be in the same tense + the participle: …were planted…
3. Add “by” + the doer (or leave it out): …by our class.
cards.note: Ten trees were planted by our class.

cards.title: Passive → active
cards.text:
The trophy has been won by them.
1. The doer after “by” moves to the front: They…
2. Make the verb active, same tense: …have won…
3. The old subject goes after the verb: …the trophy.

cards.title: Pronouns switch jobs
cards.body: A subject pronoun (I, he, she, we, they) that moves behind “by” becomes an object pronoun (me, him, her, us, them): “He helped me” → “I was helped by him.” And the other way round: “by them” at the front becomes “They…”.

cards.title: The verb agrees with its new subject
cards.body: When the subject changes, check the verb: “The twins are washing the car” → “The car is being washed by the twins.” “The car is being washed by my brothers” → “My brothers are washing the car.”

prompts: Which pair of your sentences sounds better active, and which better passive? Why?
What three things do you check every time you flip a sentence?
